project_name: Lake Charles Chemicals Project ethane cracker
source_note: Explicit company FID. Later Sasol source states cracker achieved beneficial operation in August 2019.

Annual report states +800 million lb/year ethylene and startup 2014. FID not yet audited. V14 recovery: LyondellBasell stated that detailed engineering was in process and long-lead items had already been ordered for the 800+ million lb/yr La Porte ethylene debottleneck; the same update gave a defined capital project and completion schedule. Ordering long-lead equipment is treated as an equivalent binding capital commitment, not as a permit or later construction inference.

Annual report states +250 million lb/year ethylene and startup 2015. FID not yet audited. V14 recovery: LyondellBasell reported that the Channelview expansion furnaces had been ordered and foundations poured, with mechanical completion scheduled. The date is the first source-locked observation of project-specific equipment procurement; procurement is used as equivalent binding capital commitment.
Annual report states +800 million lb/year ethylene and expected/startup 2016. FID not yet audited.

Explicit company FID; integrated complex also includes approximately 1.6 mtpa polyethylene output. Main construction start separately verified. Capacity repair at final freeze audit: Shell 2024 Form 20-F reports Monaca ethylene capacity of 1,500 thousand tonnes/year. Capacity source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1306965/000130696525000007/shel-20241231.htm
Company states project first announced March 2011 and board approved execution on 3 Oct 2013; two 0.5 mtpa PE units are integrated downstream.

project_name: Baytown ethane cracker and Mont Belvieu polyethylene expansion
source_note: Construction start verified 19 Jun 2014; associated two 650 ktpa PE lines; cracker startup verified 26 Jul 2018. Explicit FID still unresolved.
Decision to proceed after final environmental approval; integrated 1.8 mtpa cracker and 1.3 mtpa PE capacity.
Explicit FID for 625 ktpa polyethylene unit.
LyondellBasell announced explicit final investment decision on 29 Jul 2016 for 500 ktpa Hyperzone HDPE plant. Site later confirmed as La Porte; operations began in 2020.

current_status: pre-FID / active development after partner withdrawal
source_note: Approximately $200m FEED, property option, permits and feedstock agreement documented; company explicitly states final investment decision has not been made. PTTGCA disclosed a 6-9 month delay and Daelim withdrawal on 14 Jul 2020, but subsequent company updates continued to describe the project as active and pre-FID. A June 2022 update stated no FID was imminent, while discussions with potential partners continued. Capacity repair at final freeze audit: PTTGC America project facts state proposed ethylene and derivatives capacity of 1.5 million metric tonnes/year. Capacity source: https://pttgca.com/project-facts/

project_name: Tacoma Manufacturing and Marine Export Facility
source_note: SEPA scoping began Dec 2015 for up to four 5,000 t/day lines; developer terminated Port lease effective 19 Apr 2016 after feasibility period.

project_name: Kalama Manufacturing and Marine Export Facility
source_note: Port agreement dates to Apr 2014; final supplemental EIS Dec 2020; WA Ecology denied shoreline conditional-use permit 19 Jan 2021. Capacity repair at final freeze audit: Washington Ecology SSEIS specifies 10,000 metric tonnes/day for 360 days/year = 3.6 million metric tonnes/year. Capacity source: https://apps.ecology.wa.gov/publications/documents/2006011.pdf

sponsor: Leucadia Energy / Lake Charles Clean Energy
source_note: DOE records show Phase 2 CCS support from 2010 and that Leucadia informed DOE on 24 Sep 2014 it would not pursue the main petcoke-to-methanol project. Capacity repair at final freeze audit: EPA permit-comparison record gives Lake Charles Clean Energy methanol production of 2,930,000 US tons/year; converted to approximately 2,658.1 thousand metric tonnes/year using 0.90718474 metric tonne per short ton. Capacity source: https://archive.epa.gov/region6/6pd/air/pd-r/ghg/web/pdf/celanese-resp2public-comment.pdf

2019 Louisiana announcement described renewed project with SABIC and FID still prospective. SABIC Annual Report 2019 later stated it did not see the SLM joint venture as feasible. Treat as negative resolution / partner withdrawal, not a definitive physical-project cancellation. In a 2023 air-quality filing, Koch/Ramboll states that South Louisiana Methanol submitted a permit rescission request to LDEQ on 8 Feb 2023 (LDEQ EDMS doc 13671037). Original project is therefore coded as an absorbing cancellation/permit-rescission event on that date.
Documented $800m syndicated loan facility agreement entered Mar 15 2017 with YCI Methanol One for project construction. Coded Tier 2 binding project-finance commitment; not explicit FID.

current_status: post-FID paused in 2020 then later restarted
source_note: Explicit FID 19 Jul 2019. 2020 company reporting documents temporary care and maintenance and deferred capital spending; valuable post-FID state-transition case.
Project lineage begins with CPChem/Qatar Petroleum USGC II announcement in July 2019; positive FID announced in Nov 2022 as Golden Triangle Polymers.
2012 Annual Report records July 2012 FID; later industry/company materials place first methanol in Jan 2015.
2013 Annual Report states FID reached in April 2013; Methanex Q2 2013 report corroborates decision during Q2.

OCI selected Beaumont in Nov 2013, signed basic engineering/license agreements in Feb 2014, and held groundbreaking/site-preparation commencement on 20 Mar 2014. No explicit Tier 1-2 FID/board commitment recovered; retain construction as lower-tier milestone.

Company states methanol unit was placed into service in Q4 2013 after being idle since 2004; commitment date remains unresolved. V14 recovery: LyondellBasell stated that detailed engineering had been contracted and long-lead items ordered for the Channelview methanol restart, with an approximately $150m capital cost and defined restart schedule. This is treated as equivalent binding capital commitment.

Celanese disclosed a signed Mitsui JV agreement on 15 May 2013; Q2 2013 call states major equipment was on order and construction was expected later that quarter. Coded Tier 2 binding commitment with quarter precision, not as explicit FID.
Proman group company report lists Pampa Fuels fully commissioned in 2015 at 65 ktpa; above frozen 50 kt/y inclusion floor. Decision date still unresolved.

Big Lake Fuels requested rescission of its Title V and PSD permits on 19 Feb 2024 after failing to begin construction by the extended deadline. Primary permit-rescission request now source-locks terminal negative state.
INEOS and Sasol announced MOU in July 2013 and explicit FID on 9 Jun 2014; Sasol reports beneficial operation in Nov 2017.
ExxonMobil announced the 650 ktpa Beaumont expansion in Nov 2016; 2016 earnings disclosure states construction had begun. Startup 24 Jul 2019. No explicit Tier 1-2 FID recovered.

TCEQ record states construction permit granted 8 Aug 2014 for LDPE plant as part of Point Comfort expansion. Expansion included 400 ktpa LDPE and 400 ktpa HDPE/LLDPE; dual-purpose unit started Aug 2019 and LDPE startup was delayed into 2020. Explicit FID unresolved.

Dow announced U.S. Gulf Coast performance-plastics units in Mar 2013 and location in Aug 2013; 2017 10-K records startup of new ELITE PE unit in Freeport. Capacity 400 ktpa from contemporaneous industry reporting; exact FID unresolved. V14 recovery: Dow SEC filing records the August 27, 2013 location decision and states that the ELITE polymer production unit will be built in Freeport as one of four announced U.S. Gulf Coast Performance Plastics investments. This is treated consistently with existing Tier-2 capital-investment announcement precedents.

Dow 2013 10-K identifies new LDPE unit at Plaquemine; 2018 filing confirms startup. Capacity 350 ktpa from contemporaneous project reporting; explicit FID unresolved. V14 recovery: Louisiana Economic Development and Dow announced a $1.06bn Plaquemine investment package including a new high-performance polyethylene plant and stated construction of the new polyolefins plants would begin by year-end 2013. The quantified company investment decision is treated as Tier-2 binding capital commitment.

WVDEP shows no significant site preparation as of Jan 2017. Bilfinger announced a $30m rebuilding contract on 28 Apr 2017 with work commencing immediately; this is coded as Tier 3/4 project progress, not FID. Plant opened in 2023.

Louisiana announcement explicitly states construction would follow permits and final investment decision. No source-locked later FID/startup found in this pass; retain as censored/unresolved candidate.

Permit application filed Feb 2017; air permit issued Jan 2018; FEED awarded Feb 2018. Current project site still describes facility as developing. No source-locked FID found. Current IGP project materials continue to describe the complex as under development; a 2025 Louisiana economic forecast likewise reports the FID date as unknown. Do not code a terminal event.
2014 Annual Report states a 220 million lb/year PE expansion at Matagorda was completed in Q1 2014. Announcement/FID date remains unresolved.

project_name: St. Charles bimodal gas-phase HDPE debottleneck
source_note: Dow 2016 10-K states gas-phase PE expansions were underway at St. Charles; 2018 reporting identifies 125 ktpa bimodal HDPE debottleneck and Q4 2018 completion. Explicit FID unresolved.

Braskem 2014 Form 20-F described ASCENT as a West Virginia integrated PE project still under study and subject to board approval. Project was re-evaluated in Apr 2015 under changed energy scenarios; no FID recovered.

North Dakota governor announcement described a planned 1.5 Mtpa PE facility. Later Badlands release reported technology and feedstock agreements and proposed scale increase to 2 Mtpa; no FID or construction start recovered.
Company-confirmed relocation to Ohio in Sep 2014 for roughly 600 million lb/year integrated ethylene/PE facility. Project reported on hold in Sep 2015; no FID recovered.

Dow 2016 Form 10-K states that the company completed an expansion of a gas-phase polyethylene production facility in Seadrift, Texas during 2016. A contemporaneous North America PE capacity table reports the increment as 75 ktpa, above the frozen 50 ktpa admission threshold. Exact announcement/FID date remains unresolved.

Dow SEC filing states the company announced a five-year ~$4bn investment program on May 11 2017 whose primary components included construction of a world-scale 600 ktpa U.S. Gulf Coast polyethylene facility. Coded Tier 2 explicit company capital-investment commitment; not explicit FID.

current_status: pre-FID / major construction deferred / project persists
source_note: Louisiana Economic Development announced a feasibility study on 3 Sep 2015 and explicitly stated that a future FID would determine whether the project proceeded. LDEQ permit applications followed in 2015. FG later planned two 1.2 Mtpa crackers with PE derivatives; major construction was deferred in Oct 2020. Current project materials continue to present the project as moving forward, so no cancellation is coded.

Westlake announced the broader Petro 1/Petro 2 expansion program in Apr 2011; Petro 2 work began Jan 2013 and added about 240 million lb/year (about 109 ktpa), completed Q1 2013. Explicit FID not recovered. V14 recovery: Westlake SEC filing states that in April 2011 the company announced an expansion program to increase ethylene capacity of both Petro 1 and Petro 2; it further documents that 2011-2012 capital expenditures largely related to Petro 2. The program announcement plus contemporaneous capital spending supports Tier-2 commitment for Petro 2.

project_name: Calvert City ethylene expansion and ethane conversion
source_note: Westlake company release announced the Calvert City ethylene conversion/expansion together with the PVC expansion on Oct 2 2012. Existing v12 coded the same investment package PVC component as Tier 2; ethylene component is harmonized to Tier 2 for internal consistency.

Part of Westlake Apr 2011 ethylene expansion program; Petro 1 expansion added 250 million lb/year (about 113 ktpa) and was completed in Q2 2016. Explicit FID not recovered. V14 recovery: Westlake SEC filing states that in April 2011 it announced an expansion program covering both Lake Charles ethylene units, including Petro 1. The later filing documents substantial project costs already incurred before physical execution. Consistent with the existing Westlake Tier-2 announcement precedent, April 2011 is retained as the source-locked commitment month.

project_name: Chocolate Bayou seventh furnace / ethylene capacity expansion
source_note: INEOS reports a $115m new furnace at Chocolate Bayou; contemporaneous ICIS universe table reports about 115 ktpa ethylene expansion. Announcement/FID date still unresolved.
Contemporaneous trade report explicitly states Williams board approved the Geismar expansion and gives $350-400m expected capital spending. Coded Tier 2 board approval.

Company announced 200 million lb/year ethylene availability expansion on 3 Jun 2013 after TCEQ consent; construction targeted within the next quarter; completed Dec 2014. V14 recovery: Chevron Phillips Chemical announced that it will expand Sweeny ethylene production by adding a tenth furnace, reported TCEQ consent to begin construction, and scheduled construction for the next quarter. The definitive company decision and immediately authorized execution are treated as Tier-2 commitment.

project_name: Port Arthur steam cracker 10th furnace expansion
source_note: BASF TOTAL started a 10th furnace on 24 Mar 2014; BASF investor materials identify 2014 as a capacity-expansion step. Contemporaneous ICIS universe table reports about 110 ktpa expansion.

OxyChem and Mexichem formed Ingleside Ethylene LLC on 31 Oct 2013 to build and operate the 1.2bn lb/year cracker and entered related supply agreements; treated as Tier-2 binding commitment. Commercial operations began Feb 2017.
Explicit FID on 17 Dec 2015; 1 Mtpa ethylene cracker. Groundbreaking Jun 2016; Lotte held completion ceremony May 2019.
Borealis states that in 2018 the partners took the final investment decision to jointly build the 1 Mtpa ethane cracker. Commercial operations started 21 Jul 2022.

Formosa CSR identifies a new Texas ethane cracker with 1.2 Mtpa ethylene and projected Q1 2019 completion; regulator/current operations confirm Olefins 3 later operating. Explicit FID and exact startup month remain unresolved. V14 recovery: Formosa Plastics corporate history states that in 2014 its Board of Directors agreed to establish Formosa Industries Corporation in the U.S. to invest in a 1.2 Mt/y ethane cracker and a 400 kt/y HDPE plant. The board action directly satisfies Tier 2; only year precision is recoverable from the source.

Dow announced restart as part of 2011 Gulf Coast investments; cracker restarted at end-Dec 2012. Capacity benchmark about 400 ktpa from contemporaneous ethylene project table. V14 recovery safety-margin audit: Dow's Q1 2012 Form 10-Q, filed 2012-05-02, describes the St. Charles ethylene cracker restart as the first project in a set of announced U.S. Gulf Coast investments, with completion expected by year-end 2012. To avoid back-dating the commitment to the preliminary April 2011 'finalizing plans' announcement, v14 uses the SEC filing date as the first source-locked public Tier-2 confirmation of the capital investment. This is not inferred from the later restart/startup date.
Braskem states board formally approved FID; 450 ktpa. Construction completion and commissioning announced June 24 2020.

project_type: New PP unit at existing site
source_note: ExxonMobil funding decision and later startup both explicit; 450 ktpa.

Enterprise SEC filing states that on Jan 7 2013 it executed long-term fee-based agreements that effectively sold out the 1.65 billion lb/yr PDH facility. Coded Tier 2 binding commercial commitment; not labeled FID.
Long-term fee-based contracts announced Sep 2019 to support construction; treated as Tier 2 binding commercial commitment, not explicit FID. Startup Aug 1 2023.
Project approved and announced Mar 3 2025; company later states further development was paused during 2025. Delay precision currently year only.
250m lb/yr announced in Apr 2012; later company filings refer to 265m lb/yr (~120 ktpa) and expected 2016 startup. Explicit FID and actual startup still to source-lock.

MEGlobal announced construction of the Oyster Creek MEG plant and that the project would benefit from a long-term ethylene supply agreement with Dow. Coded Tier 2 binding project-specific commercial commitment; not explicit FID.
Annual report states Shintech decided in June 2013 to increase PVC capacity by ~300 ktpa; later report records PVC completion end-2015 and VCM expansion phases.
Company says it had begun construction and first phase adds 290 ktpa PVC. Treated Tier 2 commitment because investment/construction decision is explicit, not labeled FID.
Decision to invest $1.25bn announced; +380 ktpa PVC and +580 ktpa VCM. Shintech history records PVC-2/VCM-3 expansion startup milestones through 2024.

Formosa expansion schedule confirms PP III under construction; technology announcement identifies 250 ktpa new PP unit. No Tier 1-2 FID/board date recovered; retain as source-locked physical candidate with lower-tier project progression only.

545 ktpa PDH project was part of Formosa Point Comfort expansion announced Feb 2012; thyssenkrupp technology/engineering contract dated Sep 2014; thyssenkrupp reference records completion in 2021. Explicit Tier 1-2 FID not recovered.

Formosa announced 136 ktpa PVC expansion in Dec 2017; Aug 2019 LED release records $332m investment commitment. Startup was delayed repeatedly; market reporting indicates capacity added in 2024. FID label is Tier 2 investment commitment, not explicit FID.

Westlake 2012 10-K states it announced the existing PVC plant expansion in October 2012; 200 million lb/yr (~90.7 ktpa) increment, completed 2014. Coded Tier 2 because company announced an active investment project, not an explicit FID.

Westlake explicitly announced Geismar PVC/VCM expansion in Feb 2018. Company did not split 750m-lb global PVC increment by site; later market reporting says Geismar rose from 272 ktpa to >500 ktpa, implying at least ~228 ktpa U.S. increment. Capacity field is a conservative lower bound, not an exact engineering nameplate increment.
BASF evaluated the project in May 2014, selected Freeport and 475 ktpa capacity in Mar 2015 subject to 2016 board approval, then on Jun 6 2016 explicitly postponed the final investment decision.

Honeywell UOP/industry sources documented the >1 Mtpa Ascend PDH development; ICIS reports the company shelved the planned project in Feb 2016 as the propylene/propane spread narrowed and quotes the CEO that revival was unlikely.

project_name: Odessa integrated PDH and polypropylene project
source_note: 2013 industry reporting documented a 300 ktpa Odessa PDH plan. ICIS reported on Sep 16 2015 that REXtac had cancelled the west-Texas PDH plan; later reporting says the company instead pursued PP restarts and a propylene splitter.
